 Precious Achiuwa (ankle) is probable for Wednesday’s game against the Lakers. 
 Achiuwa, who has been starting for the injured Keegan Murray (ankle), played 27 minutes in Monday’s win over the Mavericks. The probable tag suggests he’ll be available, and Achiuwa should remain in the starting lineup if so.

 Precious Achiuwa (ankle) is available to play against the Lakers on Wednesday. 
 As expected, Achiuwa will be good to go against Los Angeles. He’ll continue to start in place of Keegan Murray, who is still sidelined with an ankle injury. Achiuwa has had a couple productive outings, but he isn’t the best streaming option on a 14-game day. 
 Precious Achiuwa 
 SAC 
 Forward 
 #9 
 Precious Achiuwa contributed 24 points (12-of-17 FGs), nine rebounds, two assists and four steals on Thursday against the Pelicans. 
 For the third straight game, Achiuwa got the starting nod in place of Keegan Murray (ankle), and this was his best performance of the season. He set a new season high for scoring and nearly finished with a double-double. Murray is set to be re-evaluated in early November, but Achiuwa should have at least a few more starts, making him worth considering as a streaming option with the Kings playing four games next week. 
 Keegan Murray 
 SAC 
 Forward 
 #13 
 According to HoopsHype’s Michael Scotto, Keegan Murray (ankle) will be re-evaluated in 10-14 days. 
 Murray was held out of Sunday’s loss to the Grizzlies due to left ankle capsulitis. Precious Achiuwa moved into the starting lineup, finishing with 12 points, 10 rebounds, two steals and three blocks in 39 minutes. He’s a worthwhile pickup while Murray sits, but fantasy managers will likely take a hit in free-throw percentage.

 #9 
 Precious Achiuwa tallied 12 points (6-of-13 FGs, 0-of-6 FTs), 10 rebounds, two steals and three blocks in Sunday’s loss to the Grizzlies. 
 The Kings were without Keegan Murray (ankle) for Sunday’s game, so Achiuwa made a spot start. While his foul shooting was a disaster, the positives outweighed that negative in terms of the Kings forward’s production. Achiuwa played 39 minutes against the Grizzlies and recorded a double-double with five “stocks.” Sacramento plays three games in Week 2, starting with the Spurs on Tuesday, and Achiuwa would be a worthwhile pickup if Murray remains out.

 Precious Achiuwa 
 SAC 
 Forward 
 #9 
 Precious Achiuwa got 14 points (7-of-11 FGs), six rebounds, an assist and a steal on Friday against the Blazers. 
 This performance is obviously influenced by a lot of shot attempts and good efficiency from Precious. He won’t do this every game, but he will have the occasional game where he will score really well. If you want to use him as a streamer only, he could be worth taking a look at if you need some points and rebounds. Do not expect much more than that however. 
 Keegan Murray 
 SAC 
 Forward 
 #13 
 Keegan Murray accounted for two points (1-of-8 FGs), four rebounds and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Clippers. 
 Given Darius Acuff Jr.'s struggles on Wednesday, Murray’s night may avoid some scrutiny. However, he also struggled, missing his first seven attempts and not scoring until 9:08 was left in the fourth quarter. And Murray didn’t do much in the other categories either, which is a concern for fantasy managers. He’ll look to bounce back on Friday when the Kings host Portland.

 Klay Thompson finished Wednesday’s overtime win over the Clippers with 30 points (11-of-22 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, one block and eight three-pointers.
 Thompson had his best game of the season on Wednesday, shooting 8-of-17 from beyond the arc. His last three-pointer was the most important, as the Heat guard/forward hit one from the left corner with one second remaining in overtime to give Miami the win. Inconsistent in his first five games, Thompson has scored at least 19 points in three straight. Could he be returning to fantasy relevance? The Heat play two more games this week, so it may not be a bad time to stream Klay if you need three-pointers. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Naji Marshall produced 22 points (9-of-12 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs.
 The Mavericks had no answer for Victor Wembanyama and looked set to get blown out. However, Marshall got going in the second half, shooting 7-of-9 from the field and scoring 17 points. Marshall remains a player who can be rostered in deep leagues, even though he’ll come off the bench on most nights.

 Cooper Flagg finished Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs with 19 points (7-of-19 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), 10 rebounds and five assists.
 After shooting 3-of-19 from the field in Monday’s loss to the Kings, Flagg got off to a terribly slow start on Wednesday. The reigning Rookie of the Year missed all seven of his shots in the first quarter and started 1-of-11 from the field. The good news is that Flagg shot 6-of-8 the rest of the way. Add in the rebounds and assists, and the final stat line was solid, but category managers would have wanted to see more defensive stats.
